Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

idea noun

a plan

also good idea, I have an idea, you’re full of ideas, full of ideas, resourceful

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.36: cōnsilium est aliquid faciendī aut nōn faciendī excōgitāta ratiō (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. idea: optimum cōnsilium, a great idea
Traupman 330
Traupman 331

cōnsilium, cōnsiliī n.

noun, second declension

an idea of what to do, a plan

Other words

  • in mentem venit — it occurs to (someone); I’ve had an idea

    phrase: the person in the dative; the thing as subject, or impersonal with a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.36.1: sī quid in mentem veniet; Cic. Rosc. Am. 95: venit enim mihi in mentem ōris tuī (Lewis & Short)

    In Cicero the subject is a neuter pronoun or rēs; otherwise the verb is impersonal, with a genitive (Lewis & Short).

  • plēnus cōnsiliī — full of ideas, resourceful

    plēnus with the genitive · also used · classical · Plaut. Ep. 1.2.49 (Lewis & Short), s.v. plēnus; Traupman 101: plēnus (-a) cōnsiliī es; Traupman 331

  • idea, ideae f. — a Platonic Idea, an archetype

    noun, first declension · avoid · classical · Sen. Ep. 58 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. idea

    Seneca’s loan for Plato’s Idea; Cicero writes the word in Greek (Lewis & Short). It never means a plan or a passing thought, and Morgan–Owens gives idea only in the Platonic sense, marked as a modern word.

Examples

  • Semper cōnsilium tunc deest, cum opus est maximē.

    Good ideas are always missing just when they are most needed.Publ. S 31

  • Sērō in perīclīs est cōnsilium quaerere.

    It is too late to look for a plan in the middle of danger.Publ. S 62

  • Probum cōnsilium!

    Good idea!Traupman 140

See also idea, plan, suggest, decision.
